tools.name: search_haystack_docs
tools.description:
Search the official Haystack framework documentation (https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai) for components, pipelines, integrations, and APIs. Returns relevant documentation sections with source URLs — use before writing, modifying, or explaining any Haystack code.

Use this tool BEFORE answering any question about Haystack or writing Haystack code. Do not rely on training data — the framework evolves rapidly and APIs change between versions.

Query strategy:
- Prefer specific class names (`OpenSearchBM25Retriever`, `ConditionalRouter`, `MarkdownHeaderSplitter`) or integration names (`weaviate`, `qdrant`) over generic terms like "retriever" or "splitter".
- For conceptual questions, phrase as a concrete task ("split markdown preserving code blocks") rather than a single keyword.
- If the top results don't answer the question, reformulate with synonyms and search again (e.g. "document store" vs "docstore", "generator" vs "LLM", "similarity ranker" vs "reranker").

Filtering (optional `filters` input):
- Narrative documentation only (guides, tutorials, how-tos): `{"field": "meta.type", "operator": "==", "value": "documentation"}`
- API reference only (class signatures, parameters): `{"field": "meta.type", "operator": "==", "value": "api-reference"}`
- Default is no filter (searches everything). Only filter when the user's question is unambiguously about one kind of content — for signature/parameter lookups, prefer API reference; for explanations or "how do I", prefer documentation.

Citation:
- Always include the result's `meta.url` when quoting or summarizing, so the user can read the full page.
- When answering from multiple sources, cite each one.

filters.description:
Provided to the 'bm25_retriever' component as: 'Filters applied to the retrieved documents. The way runtime filters are applied depends on
the `filter_policy` specified at Retriever's initialization.', and Provided to the 'embedding_retriever' component as: 'Filters applied when fetching documents from the Document Store.
Filters are applied during the approximate kNN search to ensure the Retriever returns `top_k` matching
documents.
The way runtime filters are applied depends on the `filter_policy` selected when initializing the Retriever.'.
